turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Hey dragon. I'm seeing miss Russell. She's a 39-year-old female here for, what are you here for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's my right upper arm. It hurts really, really bad.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So severe right upper arm pain.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I was playing volleyball yesterday, uh last night. Um and I went to spike the ball, and the team we were playing, they're dirty. So um, somebody right across from me kinda kicked my legs from under me as I was going up, and I fell and landed on my arm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Mm-hmm, like right on your shoulder.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Um, so this happened, what? Like 12 hours ago now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, seven o'clock last night, so a little more than that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you taken anything for the pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've been taking ibuprofen every six hours I think, but it's really not helping at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, what would you rate your pain?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And do you have any medical problems?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Do you take any medicine for it?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. And any surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I had a lumbar fusion about six years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right. Let's uh, let's look at your x-ray. Hey dragon. Show me the last radiograph. So this is looking at your right arm, and what I see is a proximal humerus fracture. So you kinda think of your humerus as a snow cone, and you knocked the-

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The top of the snow cone?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: The top off the snow cone. Um, so I'll be gentle but I want to examine your arm.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: All right. Are you able to straighten your arm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I can just straighten the elbow as long as I don't move up here.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: As long as you don't move your shoulder.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Go ahead and bend. Okay. So your exam is generally normal, meaning that the rest of your body is normal

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: But you've got some swelling and erythema-

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: . On that right shoulder. You've got uh, tenderness over your right shoulder. You've got normal pulses, and everything else is normal. Any numbness or tingling in that right arm?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, so what we're going to have to do- the good thing about um, these kinds of fractures is generally, they will heal up without surgery. Um, but we have to put you in a sling that weighs your arm down and pulls it down. So we're going to put you in a long arm cast and a sling, and then we're gon na check you in two weeks to see if those bones have realigned and if they haven't, then we're gon na have to talk about doing surgery at that time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I'm going to prescribe you some pain medicine. We'll do lortab 500- lortab 5 milligram. Um, you can take one to two tablets every uh, six hours as needed for pain. I'll give you 20 of those.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And um, do you have any allergies to medicines? I didn't ask.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't have no allergies.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay. Um, hey dragon, go ahead and order any medications or procedures discussed. Um, do you have any questions for me?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Okay, great. Why don't you come with me, we'll get the tech to put the cast on.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And we'll get you checked out.
